Home
Courses
Trading Decisions and Behaviour
Beginner
Trading Decisions and Behaviour

Understand decision biases, review assumptions and practise reflective exercises.

Includes 5 lessons, quizzes, sources, and a completion badge. The $100,000 simulator supports spot instruments; options and futures contract mechanics are worksheet exercises.

Published by TradeHQ, created by Anuga Weerasinghe. Publisher background and editorial approach. No independent professional review is claimed; any recorded source-check scope appears on the page.

Your progress
0%
Earn the
Trading Psychology Completion
badge on completion

This educational track examines research on decision biases alongside fictional trading examples. It introduces optional records and checklists that can support reflection, without claiming professional consensus or a link to profitable performance.

What you'll be able to do
Name the specific biases most likely to affect your own decisions, with an example from your own trade log.
Recognise when a fictional trading scenario invites an impulsive decision and consider alternatives including not trading.
Keep a record of assumptions before evaluating a hypothetical outcome; compare facts with interpretations.
Create an optional preparation and review checklist with no fixed time requirement.
Distinguish between a losing trade that followed the plan and a winning trade that broke it.
Before you start

No previous trading is required. All exercises can be completed with made-up data and virtual observations, without real transactions.

How the lessons build on each other

The sequence explores possible decision biases, reactions to an outcome, a journal as an observation record, optional checklists and portfolio-drawdown arithmetic. It does not constitute psychological assessment or a tested method for earning returns.

Who this track is not for

This track does not address clinical mental health, gambling addiction or financial distress, and it is not a substitute for professional support. If trading is causing you real financial or psychological harm, please speak to a qualified professional rather than reading another lesson on discipline.

Lessons
LESSON 1
Cognitive Biases in Trading Decisions
Confirmation bias, anchoring and loss aversion offer ways to examine decisions without assuming a universal emotional response.
9 min
LESSON 2
Revenge Trading & Tilt — Recognising Unplanned Decisions
Tilt is the emotional state where a trader tries to recover a loss immediately with larger, unplanned trades.
8 min
LESSON 3
A Trading Journal: Observations and Limits
Use a decision record to review assumptions without claiming it proves profitable skill.
8 min
LESSON 4
Optional Checklists for Practice Sessions
Prepare and review educational exercises without prescribing a professional routine or profitable outcome.
8 min
LESSON 5
Understanding Drawdowns in a Simulation
Calculate declines from a previous portfolio peak and compare hypothetical sizing and recovery assumptions.
8 min
Completion badge

Trading Psychology Completion: Awarded after completing every lesson in the Trading Psychology Mastery track. Educational simulation only — not financial advice.

All courses

Educational simulation only — not financial advice. Virtual money; no brokerage transactions. Quotes may be delayed, cached, unavailable or fixed simulator values; generated charts are labelled separately. Practice results do not predict investment outcomes.

TradeHQ is an educational paper trading simulator. No real money is traded. Nothing on this website constitutes investment, financial, legal or tax advice. Past simulated performance does not predict future real-world performance.
